misconceptions.description: Writing a subject line like 'Concern' or 'Hello' that does not name the topic or the student
misconceptions.trigger: subject line has no specific topic, student name, or date
misconceptions.feedback: A subject line must name the topic so the reader knows what the message is about before opening it. 'Concern' tells them nothing.

misconceptions.description: Filling the body with vague worry ('some issues lately') instead of one dated, concrete fact
misconceptions.trigger: email body has no specific date, count, or named item
misconceptions.feedback: Replace vague phrases with one concrete fact: which assignment, which dates, how many. Vague concern alarms without informing.

misconceptions.description: Ending with 'we should discuss at some point' instead of a specific action and deadline for the reader
misconceptions.trigger: message asks the reader to do nothing specific by no specific time
misconceptions.feedback: State exactly what you want the reader to do and by when. 'At some point' is not an action the reader can take.
